items: AKWA IBOM STATE (PSI 9.1): Governor Umo Eno Declares Education Emergency, Approves 2,000 Teachers and School Grants
OGUN STATE (PSI 9.0): Ogun State Government Disburses ₦3.503 Billion Severance Allowances to Former LG Officials
YOBE STATE (PSI 9.0): Governor Buni Approves Employment of Over 1,000 Medical Students and Wage Upgrades
LAGOS STATE (PSI 8.9): Lagos Receives Sierra Leone President, Launches EPPPS Planning, LASCOPA Helpline & LSWMO Actions
KADUNA STATE (PSI 8.8): Governor Uba Sani Receives Pensioners Union After Disbursing Over ₦21.4 Billion
KATSINA STATE (PSI 8.7): World Bank Moves to Adopt Katsina Community Development Framework; Scholars Back Gov Radda
ONDO STATE (PSI 8.5): Governor Aiyedatiwa Receives NEMA Briefing and Deploys Resources to Air Force Crash Site
EDO STATE (PSI 8.4): Governor Okpebholo Threatens Contractor Arrest and Directs 24-Hour Abduction Rescue
ZAMFARA STATE (PSI 8.3): Governor Lawal Joins FG Ethiopia Mission; RUWATSAN Trains Pit Emptiers in Gusau
TARABA STATE (PSI 8.2): Governor Agbu Kefas Attends High-Level Lake Chad MNJTF Security Forum in Abuja
EKITI STATE (PSI 8.1): Ekiti Cassava Output Crosses 2.1 Million Metric Tonnes Amid Agricultural Expansion
NIGER STATE (PSI 8.1): Governor Bago Advocates NELFUND Expansion, Presents 34-Seater Bus to Niger Tornadoes FC
KEBBI STATE (PSI 8.0): Governor Idris Approves ₦63.65 Million Registration Fees for 67 Law School Indigenes
GOMBE STATE (PSI 7.8): Gombe Scores 80 Points in OGP National Assessment for Open Governance Progress
DELTA STATE (PSI 7.6): Delta State Security Operations Rescue Kidnap Victim and Arrest Five Suspects
CROSS RIVER STATE (PSI 7.5): Governor Otu Inspects Odukpani Fire Devastation and Landslide Sites to Direct State Relief
PLATEAU STATE (PSI 7.2): Plateau Government Establishes Verification Centre at PS-DMCMA to Check Substandard Goods
ADAMAWA STATE (PSI 6.8): Adamawa Governor Fintiri Directs New Operational Hilux Vehicle to Ministry of Energy
BENUE STATE (PSI 6.7): Benue State Government Issues Two-Week Ultimatum to Unauthorized Billboard Operators
OSUN STATE (PSI 6.5): Osun Environmental Sanitation Taskforce Engages Market and Religious Leaders in Osogbo
KWARA STATE (PSI 5.8): Governor AbdulRazaq Congratulates UNILORIN on Top Research Ranking in Times Higher Education
NASARAWA STATE (PSI 5.2): Governor Abdullahi Sule Hosts Solomon and Mary Lar Leadership Institute Delegation

AKWA IBOM (PSI 9.1): Governor Umo Eno declared a state of emergency in education, approving 2,000 primary teacher recruitments, a ₦50k annual teacher wardrobe allowance, and ₦500k grants to 1,776 private schools.
OGUN (PSI 9.0): Disbursed ₦3.503bn to clear inherited outstanding severance liabilities owed to 1,042 former local government political office-holders across 2016–2024 tenures.
YOBE (PSI 9.0): Approved civil service employment for 294 medical students and 801 health science trainees, alongside CATA/EAA allowances across 8 tertiary institutions and CONMESS/CONJUSS upgrades.

LAGOS (PSI 8.9): Hosted Sierra Leone President Bio, launched the Electronic Physical Planning System, introduced a 24/7 LASCOPA helpline, sealed 14 polluting properties via LSWMO, and distributed LAWMA bins.
KADUNA (PSI 8.8): Received Pensioners Union leadership following ₦3.959bn late-September release (reaching ₦21.455bn for 9,683 retirees), announced pension increases, and donated land and a bus.
KATSINA (PSI 8.7): Revealed World Bank plans to adopt Katsina's Community Development Programme as a national model, met with Scholars Association, and flagged off Matazu LGA empowerment scheme.
ONDO (PSI 8.5): Received NEMA leadership in Akure and deployed swamp buggies, local boats, and multi-agency emergency recovery assets to the Air Force aircraft crash site in Igbokoda.
EDO (PSI 8.4): Issued 48-hour contractor arrest threat over abandoned Benin-Abraka road, directed 24-hour joint security rescue of 90-year-old abducted elder, while Egor LGA swore in 10 appointees.
ZAMFARA (PSI 8.3): Joined VP Shettima's Ethiopia mission on subnational child nutrition, while RUWATSAN, UNICEF, and UK Aid trained manual pit emptiers to eradicate open defecation.
TARABA (PSI 8.2): Participated in a 2-day security forum at the National Defence College, Abuja, to align subnational intelligence with MNJTF counter-insurgency operations.
EKITI (PSI 8.1): Expanded crop cultivation acreage across rice, maize, and cassava, driving state cassava output past 2.1m metric tonnes and boosting regional food security.
NIGER (PSI 8.1): Urged Senate Committee to expand NELFUND student loans to state polytechnics/colleges, presented a 34-seater bus to Niger Tornadoes FC, and met mine collapse delegation.
KEBBI (PSI 8.0): Approved ₦63.65m to cover full tuition fees for 67 Kebbi indigenes admitted into the Nigerian Law School, disbursing ₦950k directly per student.
GOMBE (PSI 7.8): Achieved an 80-point score in the Q3 2026 Open Government Partnership Nigeria assessment, citing digital procurement publishing and participatory budgeting.
DELTA (PSI 7.6): Rescued a 25-year-old kidnap victim unharmed, arrested 5 suspects linked to cult killings and abduction, and recovered a Beretta pistol in joint raids.
CROSS RIVER (PSI 7.5): Governor Otu inspected fire destruction at Odukpani commercial hub and active Calabar landslide sites, committing to immediate SEMA relief and engineering controls.
PLATEAU (PSI 7.2): Opened a Public Information and Verification Centre at PS-DMCMA to enable citizens and distributors to verify NAFDAC codes on food, drugs, and cosmetics.
ADAMAWA (PSI 6.8): Provided a new Hilux operational vehicle to Ministry of Energy technical engineers for field monitoring of off-grid solar mini-grids across 21 LGAs.
BENUE (PSI 6.7): BIRS, Signage Agency, and Urban Board issued a two-week grace period to October 20 for outdoor advertisers to regularize permits before enforcement removal.
OSUN (PSI 6.5): Convened market, religious, and transport leaders to enforce Thursday market sanitation hours and ban refuse dumping in waterways to prevent flooding.
KWARA (PSI 5.8): Congratulated UNILORIN management as the university emerged 1st in Nigeria for research quality in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2027.
NASARAWA (PSI 5.2): Hosted a delegation from the Solomon and Mary Lar Leadership Institute at Government House, Lafia, accepting a keynote invitation for their learning academy launch.
